scalars.scalar_value: Three years of full-time, paid experience in financial management involving fiscal analysis and planning AND

items.item_text: Three years of full-time, paid experience in financial management involving fiscal analysis and planning AND
One year of experience in a college or university financial aid office responsible for office operations
Two years of supervisory experience (may be concurrent)
Plans, organizes, and oversees the processing of financial aid applications. (E)
Serves as the Financial Aid Director, in the absence of the Director, ensuring compliance with federal and state statutes and regulatory requirements. (E)

Provides leadership, supervision, and administrative oversight for the District’s Financial Aid. Federal Work-Study, and Job Placement programs in alignment with institutional mission, equity goals, and student success priorities. (E)
Develops and maintains policy and procedure manuals to ensure accurate and timely financial aid processing from application to disbursement. (E)
Supervises and evaluates assigned staff. Identified training needs of assigned staff and recommends or develops appropriate development and training plans. (E)
Coordinates the reconciliation of federal, state, and institutional financial aid programs. (E)
Coordinates responses to audits, federal and state program reviews, and internal compliance reviews. (E)
Coordinates response to escalated student issues. (E)
Organizes financial aid outreach in response to requests by local schools and community organizations and campus partners. (E)
Maintains security of personally identifiable information (PII) and student financial aid records according to federal regulations. (E)
Utilizes standard office software and specialized financial aid systems (e.g., ED Express,
COD, NSLDS, Web grants, National Student Clearinghouse) to generate reports,
track awards, make data updates, changes, and corrections, and ensure regulatory
compliance. (E)
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Equity-based principles and leadership in higher education.
Manage access to federal, state and other required sites for assigned staff.
Higher education in community colleges, including the mission of the California Community Colleges.
Investigate and resolve issues related to student eligibility and disbursement.

Federal, state, and local laws and regulations applicable to student financial aid and student services, including Title IV, Title V, California Education Code, FERPA, and related compliance requirements.
Promote financial aid awareness through participation in outreach, recruitment activities, and community engagement.
Management of the District's financial aid programs.
Attend and participate in relevant workshops, conferences, and professional development events.
Equity-minded leadership, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices, and culturally responsive service delivery in community colleges.
Supervise and evaluate staff in a fair manner while demanding the highest level of performance.
Student services program planning and evaluation, including alignment with Institutional, Program, and Student Learning Outcomes.
Handle difficult and problem students in a multicultural, multilingual environment.
Federal and state reporting requirements for financial aid programs, including audits, program reviews, FISAP, PPA renewals, Gainful Employment, SSARCC, and related submissions.
Manage complex financial aid programs.

Financial aid administration and oversight, including federal, state, institutional, and private aid programs; needs analysis methodologies; awarding, disbursement, reconciliation, and return-of-funds processes.
Learn and understand federal and state regulations and apply them to office policies and procedures.
Regulations, rules, and institutional systems, policies, and processes related to financial aid, including their connection to admissions, registration, and accounting.
Stay current on federal and state laws and regulations; recommend procedural changes as required; inform other staff of regulatory changes as they occur.
Federal, state, and local regulations, policies, and procedures for awarding and administering financial aid.
Perform a multitude of high volume, complex tasks simultaneously.
Institutional policies relevant to admissions, registration, and student accounts receivable.
Evaluate office systems and develop appropriate policies and procedures.
Federal reporting requirements for financial aid, including filing reports, making corrections, and verifying approvals.
Perform work requiring the highest level of detail and accuracy.
Effective collaboration, communication, and consensus-building techniques.
Organize and prioritize work appropriately to meet deadlines and completion expectations.
Principles and practices of management, supervision, and training.
Work independently with little direction.
Office systems, procedures, and equipment, including personal computers, student information databases, word processing, and spreadsheet applications.
Equitably develop, plan, organize, and programs, policies, and procedures to meet student, staff, and community needs.
Specialized financial aid databases and data management systems.
Approach challenges as opportunities and utilize data to inform equitable solutions that meet multiple ends.
Student eligibility criteria and application processes.
Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner; and meet critical time deadlines.
Budget development and fiscal management.
Prepare comprehensive narrative and statistical reports.
Financial aid software systems and reporting tools.
Coordinate operations effectively with other college units, including Admissions &
Professional standards related to student records and confidentiality.
Records, Job Placement Services, Student Services, Business Services, and Academic Affairs.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Work evenings and weekends as required.
Interpersonal skills using tact, patience, and courtesy.
Communicate and respond effectively verbally and in-writing using culturally relevant techniques.
